note: Order matters: the oldest items come first. The monthly update replaces the oldest items.

themes.name: AI at work
themes.tag: How we use it, and what we learn
deep: What is one task AI does for you now that you used to do by hand?
What is the best prompt or trick you have learned? Share it with us.
When did AI give you a wrong answer? How did you notice?
What would you never let AI do for you, even if it could?
Which AI tool do you use that most of us may not know?
How do you think AI will change your job in two years?
What is one thing you would automate tomorrow if you could?
What is a task you tried with AI that did not work at all?
How do you check that an AI answer is right?
What would make you trust AI more at work?
What is the most fun thing you have done with AI?
What is one AI skill you want to get better at?
hot: Most AI agents today are impressive demos, not reliable products.
In five years, most first drafts of code, docs and designs will come from AI.
Open models will beat closed models for most business uses.
AI will make junior roles harder to find, not easier.
Rules and regulation will shape AI more than technology will.
We should always say when AI helped write something.

themes.name: Tech we love
deep: What is the one app or tool you could not work without?
What is a keyboard shortcut or small trick that saves you time?
What is the best piece of tech you ever bought?
What old technology do you miss?
What new technology are you most excited about right now?
What tool did you try and then stop using? Why?
What is one tech trend you think is overhyped?
What gadget on your desk would you miss the most?
How do you use tech to stay focused?
What setting or feature do you think too few people use?
What is the best tech purchase you made for under 50 dollars?
What tool or app do you wish existed?
hot: Most dashboards are built once and never used again.
Most companies should buy tools, not build them.
Real-time collaboration tools have made us worse at deep work.
Most security problems are people problems, not technical problems.
Dark mode is better for everything.
We have too many tools and not enough habits.

themes.name: Lessons from work
themes.tag: Mistakes, fixes and what we learned
deep: What is a work mistake that taught you a lot?
What is the best advice you got early in your career?
When did asking for help change the result of a project?
Which project did not go as planned? What would you do differently?
What feedback was hard to hear but turned out to be right?
What would you tell a new teammate on their first day?
What is a skill you wish you had learned sooner?
What is a habit that made you better at your job?
When did you say no, and it turned out to be the right call?
What did you learn from a teammate who is very different from you?
What is a lesson you keep having to learn again?
What would you do differently in your first year at work?
hot: Technical debt is mostly a communication problem, not a code problem.
Estimating work in hours or points is mostly guessing.
A good prototype is worth more than a good spec.
Failing fast is only useful if you write down what you learned.
Most project delays start in the first week.
The best feedback is a little uncomfortable.

themes.name: Learning and skills
deep: What is the last thing you learned that made you proud?
What is the best course, book, video or podcast you found for work?
What skill do you want to learn this year?
How do you learn something new fast?
Who at work taught you something important?
What do you know well enough to teach in ten minutes?
What topic could you read about for hours?
What is something you taught yourself that surprised you?
What is the hardest thing you have learned so far?
What do you do when you feel stuck while learning?
Which mentor or teacher do you still think about?
What would you learn if you had a month off?
hot: Most work training is a waste of time.
You learn more from a bad project than from a good course.
Everyone at work should learn a little coding.
Writing well will matter more than coding well in ten years.
Teaching a topic is the fastest way to learn it.
A portfolio of real work matters more than certificates.

themes.name: Hot takes
themes.tag: Strong opinions about work and tech
deep: What is a work opinion that many people disagree with?
Which tech trend do you think is overhyped?
What meeting habit would you remove today?
What is one rule at work that you would change?
What did you change your mind about in the last year?
What is the best way to give feedback, in your view?
Which buzzword would you ban?
What popular work advice do you think is wrong?
What small thing annoys you at work?
What tradition at work would you happily end?
What trend do you secretly like, even if it is not cool?
What is the most overrated skill at work?
hot: Most meetings should be an email.
Cameras on make meetings better.
Product teams ship too many features and fix too few problems.
Slides are a bad way to share ideas.
Open-plan offices are bad for focus.
Chat is where good ideas go to disappear.

themes.name: Adventures

hot: Planning a trip is half the fun.
The best trips are the ones that go wrong.
Solo travel teaches you more than group travel.
Staying in one place beats visiting five cities in five days.
Tourist spots are popular for a reason.
Everyone should live in another country for a year.

hot: The book is almost always better than the movie.
Most series should end one season earlier.
Audiobooks count as reading.
Background music helps you focus.

Rewatching your favorites beats trying something new.

What is a bold idea you have never shared?

What is the best idea you ever had that went nowhere?
What everyday thing would you redesign?
Who is the most creative person you know? What do they do?
What would you invent to make Mondays better?
What idea from another industry could we borrow?
hot: Constraints make people more creative, not less.
Thinking alone first beats brainstorming as a group.
Most good ideas are small improvements, not big inventions.
The best ideas sound obvious once someone says them.
Following the data too closely kills bold ideas.
Every team should get a free week each quarter to try wild ideas.
